annotations.annotation_text: Page 517 opens Book 3, Chapter 3 ("The Inquest of Yawn") during the Age of Men phase. This passage continues the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession, featuring Yawn/Shaun, Mamalujo, HCE (voice), ALP (voice). The nocturnal dream-narrative layers Dublin topography, world mythology, and linguistic alchemy into polysemic prose.
sources: Campbell, Joseph and Robinson, Henry Morton. A Skeleton Key to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/skeletonkeytofin00camp
McHugh, Roland. Annotations to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/annotationstofin0000mchu_h5g8

JJDA: Finnegans Wake Genetic Edition. https://jjda.ie

annotations.annotation_text: Mid-page polysemic node on page 517 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): Joyce weaves multilingual puns across 60+ languages — etymological roots from the Contemporary Literature Press lexicons (Romanian, Scandinavian, Slavic, Classical) intersect with local Dublin speech rhythms. The Age of Men dream-logic transforms ordinary syntax into a palimpsest of global literary and mythic references.
sources: Tindall, William York. A Reader's Guide to Finnegans Wake. https://archive.org/details/readersguidetofi00tind

annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "night" on page 517 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession. During this Age of Men phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.
sources: Bishop, John. Joyce's Book of the Dark. https://archive.org/details/joycesbookofdark0000bish
